correctness.rationale: Final assessment of repairs/2/RESULT.md. The original strictness extension in RESULT.md line 39 is false as written: nonconstant Z can be supported on {0,z}, z>0, in which case m_j=Pr(Z=z)z^j for j>0 and all size vectors at fixed n,k have the same survival. This can occur even with Poisson resets when an individual hits deterministically one time unit after each renewal and t=3/2: no reset gives Z=0 and one reset in (1/2,1) gives Z=1. For example (3,1) then ties (2,2). The replacement preserves the frozen counterevidence, makes conditional independence explicit, and states positivity plus nonconstancy as a sufficient condition for general strict fixed-k order. It retains the weak order without positivity (trivial if Z=0 almost surely) and the valid covariance strictness for merger with any nonconstant Z. For the unchanged Brownian finding, the reflection principle and conditioning give the product of moments, Z>0 comes from finitely many finite excursions, and zero versus one early reset gives nonconstancy since q'(0+)=0>q'(t). Cauchy–Schwarz gives strictly increasing moment ratios and hence a strict decrease on balancing unit transfers. Every genuine merger has strictly positive increasing-powers covariance. Equality at t=0 or under permutations is unchanged. The replacement clarifies the finite-mean argument: after the last reset in the first half of a block with none in its second half, at least s reset-free time remains, not necessarily a start at x₀ at the midpoint. This gives the uniform stated geometric tail bound and finite strict mean comparisons. The frozen exact toy-law tests and Brownian schedule illustration are diagnostic; the analytic scope correction and tail argument have been checked directly.

evidence: The abstract majorization theorem orders products of block averages and derived convex orders, not arbitrary moments of first-hit survival in shared environments.
The stationary Brownian gas is conditional-iid in position under a global age; the avoidance and simultaneous-encounter papers change the reset rule, target event or host.
The remedied general moment statement explicitly requires independent individual randomness as well as iid schedules; it does not claim universal strictness or finite means.

evidence: The published independent and all-synchronized endpoint formulas already give S=m_1^n and S=m_n; Jensen gives the direction at the endpoints. The catalogue two-searcher comparison is exactly m_2>m_1².

Neither result compares, for example, (4,2,1) with (3,2,2) at fixed total and clock count. The target uses identical independent group laws and strict positivity/nonconstancy of the schedule survival to turn moment convexity into every majorization comparison.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the endpoint and the exact singleton special case. Products of sample averages do not specialize to this comparison in the inspected general theorem. The retained result is the general Brownian allocation rule, not a new moment inequality.

evidence: The target event is that all walkers survive a deadline, not first simultaneous encounter. Shared clocks make this the product of moments of one schedule-conditional survival variable, with independent environments across groups.
Gonçalves–Madrid–Ramos compare products of sample block averages by majorization; that statistic is not the group-conditional survival moment product here.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The right reduction is a moment product versus a partition, not a sample-average convex order or a first-encounter comparison. Classical moment log-convexity is a proof tool rather than an originality claim.

originality.rationale: The surviving main claim is the classification of all comparable equal-rate Brownian reset-clock group allocations and all genuine mergers. The repaired positivity qualifier and block-tail reasoning do not expand that claim. The original endpoint formulas, singleton merger overlap and classical moment inequalities are credited. No inspected result gives the whole arbitrary-partition strict deadline order on this model. This is a bounded statement-level screen, not a priority certification.
residual_risks: The bounded local and primary checks do not rule out an earlier application of moment-order inequalities to the same arbitrary reset-clock allocation model.
No novelty claim is made for the analytic inequalities, the two endpoint protocols, or their n=2 special case.

value.rationale: In the repaired theorem, clock sharing is a real design choice that leaves each searcher's marginal dynamics fixed. The exact optimal and worst partitions at a fixed clock budget and the direction of any merger follow for every deadline and rate, rather than just for a fitted example, an endpoint or an optimized mean. This is useful even though the proof uses elementary inequalities. The general strictness qualification prevents misapplying the same budget rule to search processes with identically tied positive moments; the main value remains the strict Brownian ordering.
